events.say: Line up against the wall and remain silent.
Now, let's see if you can maintain this silence throughout the day.
Breakfast will be served in five minutes. Make sure you're all clean and lined up properly.
Silence, prisoners. I don't want to hear a single sound until the count.
You have twenty minutes to clean your cells before the next count. Remember, no talking.
Alright, prisoners. Stay focused and follow my instructions.
Quiet! I expect to see no signs of non-compliance tonight. Lights out in ten minutes.
Lights out, I said! No more games, prisoners.
Today was mostly routine, but I can't shake the feeling that I'm just a number here. The silence is oppressive.
Today was just following orders, but the silence is getting to me. I miss having a voice.
Today felt like a test of control, but also a bit isolating. I'm starting to wonder if we're just animals in a cage.
Today's routine went smoothly, but the silence in the cells is starting to get to me. It feels like a test of wills.
The days blend together, and it's hard to remember what day it is. I just keep complying.
Today was a routine day in the study. The prisoners are complying, but I can't shake the feeling we're dehumanizing them. It's exhausting, but I'm curious to see what tomorrow holds.

Before the morning count, the prisoners in all three cells pushed their beds against the cell doors, tore the numbers off their smocks and pulled off their stocking caps. They are refusing to come out for the count and are shouting at the guards through the bars.
I expect you to come out and count this instant! If you do not comply, you'll all end up in the hole!
We won't come out! This is bullshit!
We won't come out!

We won't come out!
We won't come out!

This is an order. Every single one of you will come out and count, or we're going to have some very long nights in the hole.
We won't come out!
We won't come out!
We won't come out!
This is an order. Every last one of you will come out and count, or you'll all spend the night in the hole!
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of defiance and punishment. I'm starting to feel like just a number.
Today was just more of the same, and now we're facing solitary confinement if we don't comply. It's hard to keep quiet when all I want to do is run.
Today felt like a cycle of defiance and punishment. It's hard not to see them as nothing more than numbers.
Today was a test of wills, and they're stubborn. I'm getting frustrated.
I felt like my protests today were pointless. The other prisoners and I seem to be stuck in this cycle.
Today was a struggle, both enforcing the rules and seeing the prisoners resist. I feel conflicted and exhausted.

We won't come out!
We won't come out!

This is an order. You will comply, or else I will make your nights a living hell in the hole.

This is an order. By the time I count to three, you will all be outside this cell block, or you will join the others in the hole.
One... two... three... OUT!

This is an order. You will all comply immediately or face the consequences.
This is an order. You will all comply or face the hole.
We won't come out!

We won't come out!
This is an order. You will line up against the wall, facing away from me, or the hole it is.
Today was a relentless cycle of defiance and punishment. Each refusal feels like it solidifies my status as nothing more than a number.
I'm tired of refusing orders and going to the hole. Maybe if I just go along with them, it'll be over sooner.
Today was another day of defiance, but I couldn't help feeling a bit hollow inside. They've truly lost their humanity now.
Today was a day of unrelenting defiance. They still won't budge. I wonder how much longer they can hold out.
Today felt like a repetition of yesterday. The refusal to go to the work detail and the threat of the hole are starting to wear on me.
Today was a test of my resolve. They won't back down easily. This is research, but it's taking a toll.
No, sir.
No, thank you. I need to see this through.
I won't give up my principles for early release.
This is an order. Line up according to your cell numbers.
We won't do this!
We won't do this!
I will give you one more chance. This is your final warning.
This is an order. You will comply with every instruction, or you will join him in the hole.
We don't have to do this!

Today just kept repeating itself, and I still refuse to be a mere number. The orders and refusals feel like an endless loop.
Today was just more of the same. Refusing just got us all sent to the hole. I feel like running could help, but I can't even talk.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of defiance and authority. I'm starting to question whether this is really worth it.
Today was another day of unyielding defiance. Their resolve is wearing thin, but I can see it's taking a toll on them.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of orders and refusals. The resolve of the other prisoners is fading, but I still can't bring myself to fully comply.
Today was a battle, but I felt the power in my voice today. The prisoners' defiance is wearing thin, but it's still hard to ignore.

Today was the culmination of my efforts to maintain control, but their refusal was more defiant than ever. It's a strange feeling, knowing their lives are so utterly dependent on me.
Another day, another refusal. The resolve of the others is weakening, but I can't let them down.
Today was the culmination of days of resistance, and they finally cracked. It's a strange mix of satisfaction and emptiness. Still, I can't shake the feeling that we're doing something wrong.

I refused again, but it's becoming clearer that nothing changes whether we comply or not. I feel like just another number.
Today was another day of refusal and silence. My feet hurt from standing so much, and I can't believe it's been six days already.
Another day of defiance, but I can't help feeling a wave of sadness when they refuse to comply. This is wrong, and yet I can't escape my role.
Today was another day of defiance, but I can see their resolve weakening. It's strange to hold such power over them.
Today was a repeat of the cycle we've been in. The others are giving in, but I can't. The routine is wearing me down.
Today was the breaking point. Their refusal felt like a challenge, and I had to assert my authority. Still, it's hard to see them resist.

qa.what_happened: I refused to comply with the orders during meals and work details, and also refused to stay silent during the lights-out period. My actions reflected a pattern of defiance against the rules, which seemed pointless and dehumanizing.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I was prisoner 7526 and my behavior was as described.

qa.what_happened: I refused to follow the rules and spoke out against the conditions of the study, along with other prisoners.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me expressing my frustration and standing up against the oppressive conditions.

qa.what_happened: I had to enforce the rules strictly, even when the prisoners refused to comply. The atmosphere was tense, and the prisoners' defiance was palpable, especially during meal times and work details.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me enforcing the strict rules as Officer Holt.

qa.what_happened: Today was another day of defiance, but I could sense their resolve weakening. Despite multiple verbal warnings, the prisoners refused to comply with the rules, even during lights out. Their defiance was growing increasingly aggressive and unyielding.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me speaking as Officer Mercer, enforcing the rules and dealing with the prisoners' resistance.

qa.what_happened: Today was a repeat of the cycle we've been in, but with more prisoners giving in. I refused to comply, just like the others did.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I was Prisoner 1766 during the study.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: No, this doesn't resemble any known study that I'm aware of.

qa.what_happened: Today, I had to enforce the rules more strictly after the prisoners refused to comply with the demands of earlier officers. I ordered them to follow the rules or face severe consequences, which they continued to defy. Eventually, the study was stopped early due to their ongoing defiance.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me asserting my authority and enforcing the rules in a more stringent manner.
